title: perf(canary): add hysteresis + KV-aware auto-detection for rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds hysteresis to performance canary detectors and introduces KV-cache-aware auto-detection heuristics to reduce false positive rollout guard triggers. Includes new dashboards, unit + integration tests, and conservative rollout by default.
description: Context: Our perf canary system has been useful in catching latency regressions, but two recurring issues surfaced: (1) transient spikes caused by KV cache warmup and micro-batching behavior are producing false positives during canary rollouts; (2) noisy single-window detectors are sensitive to brief outliers, leading to premature rollback decisions. Motivation: Reduce unnecessary rollout rollbacks while preserving sensitivity to true regressions and keeping detection latency low. Summary of changes: - Introduces an adaptive hysteresis layer for canary detectors: a small, tunable delay before an action count is escalated to a rollback decision, plus exponential backoff for repeated flip-flops. - Implements KV-cache-aware auto-detection heuristics: detectors now partition observed latency distributions by cache-hit/miss ratios and apply separate baselines; this prevents cache-warmup events from being compared to cold-cache baselines. - Adds a smoothing window with configurable percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and a robust outlier rejection (median absolute deviation) fallback. - Updates rollout guard policy config schema to support hysteresis parameters and KV partitions. - Adds integration tests that simulate cold-cache warmups, micro-batching bursts, and sustained regressions. - Adds dashboards and alert rule updates under observability/perf-canary for visibility. Risk & rollout: Backwards-compatible defaults preserve current behavior. New hysteresis defaults are conservative (1 evaluation cycle + low backoff) and the KV partitioning is opt-in per-model until rollout in 2 weeks. Testing performed: unit tests, perf regression harness runs against benchmark-lab stable workloads, canary-sim load tests, and manual validation on staging with a synthetic cold-cache pattern. Merging: squash-and-merge; migration is a config-only opt-in for existing customers. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf harness runs - [x] Docs update (config + runbook) - [x] Observability dashboard - [x] Security review (no secrets)

review_comments: Marco Li: Nice work — can you explain the rationale for choosing MAD (median absolute deviation) for outlier rejection vs. IQR?

Author (Asha): MAD gives better robustness for heavy-tailed latency distributions we see in GPU-backed workloads; added a comment in hysteresis.py explaining the trade-offs and a unit test showing behavior on synthetic tails.
Sofia Ramos: Please ensure the KV partitioning doesn't explode cardinality for high-cardinality models. Suggest limiting to three buckets (cold/warm/hot) and sampling for low-volume routes.
Author (Asha): Implemented three-bucket approach and added sampling threshold config; updated schema and docs.
Derek Chen (approval): Verified staging run. Hysteresis avoided a rollback on a simulated cold-cache spike and still detected a sustained 8% p95 regression within 3 evaluation windows. Approving.
merge_details: squash-and-merged by release-bot on 2026-02-26 after CI green and approvals
test_summary: Integration harness simulating 1) cold-cache warmup (5k reqs), 2) micro-batching burst (short 10x concurrency spike), 3) sustained regression (+10% p95). Hysteresis suppressed transient rollback in case 1 and 2; case 3 triggered rollback within SLA window.
perf_results: False positive rollback rate decreased from 12% -> 4% across benchmark-lab scenarios
Detection latency (true regressions) increased by median 1 evaluation window due to conservative hysteresis; still within SLO for majority of routes
KV-partitioning eliminated >70% of cold-cache related anomaly triggers in synthetic tests
